newsitem.title: USA: IBM, Philip Morris spark big jump in blue-chips.
newsitem.headline: IBM, Philip Morris spark big jump in blue-chips.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rose sharply Monday, boosted by big gains in the shares of International Business Machines Corp. and Philip Morris Cos. Inc.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended 76.58 points higher, or 1.10 percent, at 7,008.20. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,482 to 1,031 on active volume of 459 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"The nod keeps going to the big-cap, blue-chip stocks," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
IBM and Philip Morris accounted for nearly half of the 30-stock index's rise. IBM surged 6 to 143-5/8, and Philip Morris rose 6-1/8 to 135-1/4.

The blue-chip market has been on a roller-coaster ride since the Dow chalked up a record close of 7,067.46 last Tuesday, falling in two straight sessions, before managing a scant four-point gain on Friday.
But as has happened with stubborn regularity lately, the brief pullback quickly attracted buyers.

"We had some sellers at the 7,000 level but they couldn't bring the market down too much," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter. "I don't think this rally's over. We have a very happy confluence of events."
That confluence includes an upbeat economy, a strong dollar and low inflation that recently has dipped to barely noticeable levels.

"You could make a case that with inflation as low as it is and, in our judgment, likely to stay low, this market could even sustain somewhat higher multiples," said James Crawford, senior vice president at Trevor Stewart Burton & Jacobsen Inc.
But one strong session did not throw all Wall Street's caution to the wind. Crawford, for one, still believes large-name stocks in particular are due for a pause.
"We're probably close to a point where the market is in a short-term toppy area," he said. "It would be healthy to see some of this money spread out."

Semiconductor stocks got a boost when Merrill Lynch recommended that investors take advantage of recent weakness in the group, saying Micron Technology Inc. and Texas Instruments Inc. offered the best upside opportunities.
Micron shares rose 2-1/2 to 36-7/8, and Texas Instruments climbed 2-3/4 to 82-1/8. Intel Corp. reversed course after several losing sessions, gaining 2-7/8 to 149-1/4.

Paper stocks also performed well, after Morgan Stanley upgraded three companies in the sector. Each of the three posted solid gains: Consolidated Papers Inc. rose 2 to 50-3/4, Mead Corp. gained 2-5/8 to 60, and Champion International Corp. climbed 2-1/4 to 44-1/4.

Pixar Animation Studios Inc. surged 6-7/8 to 21 on news that it would jointly produce five movies with Walt Disney Co. Disney also announced it would acquire a 5 percent stake in Pixar. Disney rose 3/8 to 75-3/4.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 10.76 points to 1,345.08.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 8.51 to 810.28. The American Stock Exchange index rose 0.78 to 598.07.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 3.74 to 424.48. The average share was up 36 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,727.40, up 58.438 or 0.76 percent.
